findings.title: Copy-paste null-check validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: In AccessTokenContext constructor line 73 is Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); It checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. As a result a null rawTokenId is accepted and stored, causing an NPE later in encodeTokenId when concatenating ':' + rawTokenId, and a null grantType failure reports the wrong message. Fix to requireNonNull(rawTokenId).

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party provider that implements OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and existing deployed jars will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut(). This is an incompatible SPI change. It should be a default method returning e.g. UNKNOWN/"na" or a derived value.

findings.title: Context constructor dereferences formParams without null check
findings.body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor the new line this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) assumes formParams is non-null. If any caller constructs a Context with null formParams, token requests fail with NPE before grant processing. Add a null guard and fall back to null/UNKNOWN grant type.

findings.title: Removed Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API compatibility
findings.body: The diff deletes the public copy constructor Context(Context context) without deprecation or replacement. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile or link (NoSuchMethodError). The constructor should be retained and updated to also copy the new grantType field.

findings.title: Unchecked cast to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory causes startup ClassCastException
findings.body: In postInit and getGrantTypeByShortcut the code casts every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without instanceof check. A custom grant factory written against the old interface (only ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType>) will cause a ClassCastException during server startup, preventing boot. Guard with instanceof or lookup only factories implementing the new interface.

findings.title: initToken assumes TokenContextEncoderProvider always exists
findings.body: initToken does TokenContextEncoderProvider encoder = session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) then immediately dereferences it. If the SPI is disabled, overridden, or unavailable in tests/embedded mode, getProvider returns null and every access-token creation throws NPE. Add a null fallback to the old behavior token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()).

findings.title: Lightweight determination uses session context client instead of token client
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). That is the request context client, not necessarily the client the token is being issued for (passed as realm/client to TokenManager.initToken). In flows like token-exchange where context client and target client can differ, the encoded TokenType (regular vs lightweight) will be wrong. The client should be passed explicitly.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and uses wrong offsets
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId the check if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; is backwards — it rejects matching tokens and accepts non-matching ones. It also uses substring(3,5) while the 6-char prefix layout is 0-1 session, 2-3 tokenType, 4-5 grant, so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6). The helper will pass wrong grant types and fail correct ones, hiding regressions in token-ID encoding.
